name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR
description:
The W196 S — a grand prix car with two seats. Mercedes took the desmodromic straight-eight out of the 1954 championship-winning W196, opened it from 2.5 to 3.0 litres, wrapped it in a spaceframe and a skin of magnesium-alloy Elektron, and went sports car racing with it in 1955.

It won everything it was asked to win. Moss and Denis Jenkinson took it round the Mille Miglia in 10h 07m 48s, a record that stood because the race never ran that fast again. Fangio drove the same course alone and finished second. It won the Targa Florio and the Tourist Trophy, and took the constructors' title.

At Le Mans in June, Pierre Levegh's 300 SLR went into the crowd and killed more than eighty people. Mercedes withdrew from motor racing at the end of the season and did not come back for thirty years.
author: RTM Shop
